passage: Mridul was in the back room of the village shop, using the shop phone, when a message from a stranger came. "I know where you live. I know your house near the banyan tree." His hands went cold. His mouth would not work. He did not answer. He did not delete it either. His older brother Sumit came in and saw his face. Mridul held out the phone. Sumit read it and his jaw tightened, but his voice stayed steady. "Come. We tell Papa now." Papa listened, thanked Mridul for showing him, and said there were people whose job it is to help with this.

qa.q: What did Mridul do with the stranger's message?
qa.a: He did not answer it and did not delete it.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling when the message came, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He was scared and frozen: his hands went cold and his mouth would not work.

qa.q: What steps should a child take after such a message?
qa.a: Do not reply, keep the messages, and tell a trusted adult straight away, as Mridul did with Sumit and Papa.

qa.q: How might Sumit have felt reading the message?
qa.a: Worried and angry, since his jaw tightened, but steady enough to take Mridul to Papa at once 🤍.

grounding: Illustrates a child frozen by a stranger's message claiming to know where he lives who keeps it, does not reply and tells a trusted adult.

passage:
Monday: A player in Vikas's racing game kept asking questions. "Which school? Which area?" Vikas ignored them and kept racing.
Wednesday: A new message appeared: "I know where you live. Nice blue gate." Vikas froze. His hands went cold. Their gate was blue. He did not type a single word. He took a screenshot, the way his cousin Pooja had once shown him, and ran to the kitchen. "Mummy, look."
Mummy read it, put down the ladle and held him tight. "You did everything right. This is not your fault." That evening she and Papa reported and blocked the account and called the cyber-crime helpline, who took down the screenshots.
Saturday: Vikas still glanced at the gate sometimes. But Papa had locked down his settings, and Vikas's chest felt looser when he played.

qa.q: What colour gate did the message mention?
What was Vikas feeling when he read the message?
qa.a: He was terrified; he froze and his hands went cold.

qa.q: Which steps did Vikas take, and why were they right?
qa.a: He did not reply, took a screenshot and told Mummy at once, so adults could report it and get help that evening.

qa.q: How did Mummy see the moment Vikas showed her the message?
qa.a: Mummy was worried but calm; she held him, told him it was not his fault and acted the same evening.

grounding: A boy frightened by a stranger claiming to know where he lives saves the message, does not answer and tells a trusted adult immediately.

passage: Tanuja, you look pale. Did something online scare you? Then listen to your Yogesh Mama first. When I was about your age, we had one computer in the corner of the hall, and I chatted on a cricket forum. One night a stranger wrote, "I know your house. Near the temple tank, isn't it?" I went stiff. I couldn't even move the mouse. And being scared was the right feeling, Tanuja; it tells you something is wrong. I didn't answer. I shouted for my father. He printed every message, sat beside me till I slept, and the next morning we went to the police station together. They took it seriously. Nothing ever happened, but I learnt to tell someone at once. So, show me what you got, and we will call your Amma right now.

qa.q: Where did the stranger claim young Yogesh lived?
How did young Yogesh feel when he read the message?
qa.a: Terrified; he went stiff and could not even move the mouse.

qa.q: What was the key choice in Mama's story, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Not replying and shouting for his father straight away; that let an adult save the messages and take them to the police.

qa.q: How might young Yogesh's father have felt that night?
qa.a: He was probably alarmed but steady, printing every message and sitting with his son before going to the police.

grounding: An uncle recalls freezing when a stranger claimed to know his house, and how not replying and telling an adult at once brought help.
